items.claim: The 5:1-5:7 bounds are byte-supported at both seams, but the row's original-language engagement misnames the song form it cites, leaves a first-in-the-book universal without a digit, and rests the closing verdict on the rendering while the verse's decisive Hebrew sound-play stays unquoted.
items.evidence: The onset run cited at oshb:Isa.5.1 re-collates at byte tier and stands verse-initial, and the rear seam holds on a verse-initial woe particle at oshb:Isa.5.8 (byte tier). Three defects. (i) The device prose cites an unpointed four-letter song form as the frame opened at that verse: unpointed is skeleton grade and is not labeled as such, and the forms actually attested there are the cohortative אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier) and the construct שִׁירַ֥ת (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier), so the cited run surfaces only as a substring inside the verb -- the contained-token class this book punishes. (ii) 'the book's first sung-frame onset' is a universal with no adjacent digit; it survives re-sweep, but only behind a homograph guard, since the one other song-skeleton site in chs 1-6 is the ornament noun at oshb:Isa.3.19, not a song frame (sweep: 9 verses book-wide at that skeleton, 1 verse for the cohortative, 2 for the construct). (iii) The closure argument quotes only the construct naming the vineyard's owner at oshb:Isa.5.7; the byte-level terminal marker of the song -- the paired assonance וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה (oshb:Isa.5.7, byte tier) -- is never quoted, and the rendering flattens both pairs into unrelated English words, so as written the closure rests on the translation. Marks: a petuchah at the preceding verse and a setumah at the span's last verse, both at the correct type, no in-span remainder.

items.claim: Both woe seams and every digit are byte-true, but the cohesion that keeps the consequence verses inside the woe is asserted from the rendering: the bytes there carry no speech verb, and the oath particle that actually binds the consequence is neither quoted nor named.
items.evidence: Verified: the onset at oshb:Isa.5.8 is verse-initial and re-collates at byte tier; the chapter's six verse-initial woe onsets (oshb:Isa.5.8, oshb:Isa.5.11, oshb:Isa.5.18, oshb:Isa.5.20, oshb:Isa.5.21, oshb:Isa.5.22) and the book-wide census re-sweep exactly as cited (sweep: 22 woe-particle verses book-wide, 6 verse-initial in this chapter); the rear seam is the verse-initial onset at oshb:Isa.5.11 (byte tier). The defect is internal: the row calls the consequence verses one divine-speech clause and states that no tier-1 seam is crossed, quoting no Hebrew for either claim. The bytes read בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם לֹ֞א (oshb:Isa.5.9, byte tier) -- a verbless construction whose speech verb is supplied by the rendering, so 'divine-speech clause' is carried by the English and not by the bytes. The elliptical oath particle spliced here is the byte-level ground that would have carried the same conclusion, and the same verse's naming of the divine source is precisely what a rival would press as an internal frame; neither is engaged. Marks: setumah at the preceding verse, petuchah at the span's last verse, both correctly typed, no in-span remainder.

items.claim: The bounds are byte-supported at both woe seams and the title-family distinction the row draws is correct, but that distinction is made in transliteration with no pointed form and misdescribes the attested epithet, while the row's real byte-level cohesion evidence goes unquoted.
items.evidence: Verified: the onset at oshb:Isa.5.11 is verse-initial, byte tier, and the rear seam is the verse-initial woe particle at oshb:Isa.5.18 (byte tier). Two defects. (i) The device prose separates a holy-God epithet from the construct Holy-One-of-Israel title using transliteration alone -- a boundary-relevant original-language claim with no quoted form, which is insufficient engagement by the standing rule. The bytes read וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.5.16, byte tier): articular and waw-prefixed, so calling it 'bare' is inaccurate, while the substantive point -- that it is a different object from the construct title standing at oshb:Isa.5.19 and oshb:Isa.5.24 -- is byte-correct and is the right hazard call. (ii) The unit's strongest byte-level cohesion evidence is unquoted: the twinned consequence particles לָכֵ֛ן (oshb:Isa.5.13, byte tier) and לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.5.14, byte tier) bind the indictment to a judgment that stays inside this row's span (sweep: 3 verses carrying that particle in this chapter, 25 book-wide), which is exactly the criterion the row needed and did not cite. Marks: no mark falls inside the span; the preceding petuchah is disclosed at the correct type, no remainder.

items.claim: Two byte-false claims about the Holy-One-of-Israel title -- a plene-only undercount and a first-appearance claim that is four chapters late -- plus an undisclosed accent-tier catchword straddling this row's rear seam.
items.evidence: The onset at oshb:Isa.5.18 and the title run at oshb:Isa.5.19 both re-collate at byte tier and sit where claimed. Three defects. (i) The digit is a plene-only needle: the plene construct returns 24 verses, and the DEFECTIVE spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier) adds a 25th, so the title census is 25 verses, not 24 (sweep: 24 plene verses + 1 defective verse); the suffixed epithet קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier) in that same verse is a different object and is not counted with it. (ii) 'here its first appearance' is byte-false: the title already stands four chapters earlier in נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier), itself a woe verse, whose rejection verb recurs at skeleton tier in the consequence at oshb:Isa.5.24 -- so this chapter carries the second and third title sites, not the first. (iii) The rear seam is straddled by a byte-true device left undisclosed: the participle closing the row, הָאֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.5.19, byte tier), recurs immediately after the woe particle of the next verse as הָאֹמְרִ֥ים (oshb:Isa.5.20, byte tier) -- identical at accent-stripped tier, differing only in accent at byte tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at accent-stripped tier, 4 at skeleton). The rendering hides it, using two different English verbs across those verses, so this continuity exists only in the bytes -- exactly the cross-seam cohesion that argues against the cut unless disclosed. Marks: the in-span setumah is disclosed at the correct type, no remainder.

items.claim: The single-verse row's self-contained-content ground is contested by the bytes: its opening participle repeats the preceding verse's closing word at accent tier, and the woe carries no announcement of judgment of its own, the governing consequence particles standing outside the row.
items.evidence: Verified clean: the onset at oshb:Isa.5.20 is verse-initial and re-collates at byte tier; the in-span setumah and the preceding one are disclosed at the correct type, no remainder. Two byte-grounded challenges. (i) The front seam is straddled: הָאֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.5.19, byte tier) closes the preceding verse and הָאֹמְרִ֥ים (oshb:Isa.5.20, byte tier) opens the indictment right after this verse's woe particle -- accent-stripped-tier identity, byte tier differing by accent alone (sweep: 3 verses book-wide at accent-stripped tier). The rendering uses two different English verbs there, so the link is visible only in the bytes and is disclosed in neither row. (ii) The rejected alternative rests on 'self-contained content', but nothing in this verse's bytes announces a consequence; in this chapter the consequence particles are לָכֵ֛ן (oshb:Isa.5.13, byte tier), לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Isa.5.14, byte tier), לָכֵן֩ (oshb:Isa.5.24, byte tier) and עַל כֵּ֡ן (oshb:Isa.5.25, byte tier) -- sweep: 3 verses carrying the first particle and 1 the second, in this chapter -- so the indictment clauses running from oshb:Isa.5.18 to oshb:Isa.5.23 are answered by one consequence at oshb:Isa.5.24-Isa.5.25, outside this row. The chapter's first two woes were each kept with their own consequence material; the same byte criterion is silently dropped here and the stack-plus-consequence rival is never disclosed.

items.claim: Onset, seams and marks are byte-clean, but the row never discloses that the verse it isolates carries no announcement of judgment at all and that the governing consequence particle stands two verses beyond its rear seam.
items.evidence: Verified: ה֖וֹי חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְנֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם נְבֹנִֽים (oshb:Isa.5.21, byte tier) is the entire verse and its woe particle is verse-initial; the rear seam is the verse-initial woe particle at oshb:Isa.5.22 (byte tier); no mark falls inside the one-verse span and the preceding setumah is disclosed at the correct type. The challenge is a non-disclosure with byte substance: the whole unit is a nominal clause -- no announcement of judgment stands in its bytes, and both witnesses render it as address-phrases only -- while the finite judgment language first enters under לָכֵן֩ (oshb:Isa.5.24, byte tier) and עַל כֵּ֡ן (oshb:Isa.5.25, byte tier), outside this row. The indictment-to-consequence construction therefore straddles the rear seam, and the rejected alternative weighs only a forward merge with the next woe, never the stack-plus-consequence rival the particles raise. Form-class labels are held rather than asserted here, no per-token parsing layer being available; the claim rests on the absence of any consequence clause in the quoted bytes plus both renderings.

Two defects. (i) The title digit repeats the plene-only sweep: 24 plene verses plus the defective קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier) makes 25 title verses (sweep: 24 + 1), so this row and its neighbour carry the same undercount. items.claim: The rear seam is argued from a chapter end plus the absence of an intervening onset while the tier-1 evidence one verse later is neither quoted nor cited, and a five-verse continuity claim runs unquoted through a doubled-token verse whose form the row declines to name.
items.evidence: Verified: the front-seam run at oshb:Isa.5.26 re-collates at byte tier, and the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.5.29 is correctly disclosed as single-witness. Three defects. (i) The rear seam's stated ground is that the chapter ends and that no further woe or frame onset intervenes -- an absence argument standing beside a division the row itself disclaims as non-cutting -- while positive tier-1 evidence sits in the very next verse: בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier), a dated frame followed by a first-person vision verb, an explicit scene-and-speaker shift. That verse is neither quoted nor carried in the row's evidence refs, so the strongest available byte ground for the seam the row wants is simply missing. (ii) The staged bytes carry a DOUBLED token pair at the ketiv/qere verse -- the unpointed ושאג (oshb:Isa.5.29, unpointed member as staged) standing beside the pointed יִשְׁאַ֨ג (oshb:Isa.5.29, byte tier) -- and the row asserts one unbroken sentence-chain running through that verse without naming which member it reads, the discipline this book requires wherever a doubled token sits inside a span being characterised. (iii) No Hebrew is quoted past the row's opening verse, so a five-verse syntactic-continuity claim is carried entirely by the rendering. The re-cited refrain chain is arithmetically right in its zone duals but carries no tier label in this row, unlike its neighbour. Marks: the in-span petuchah is disclosed at the correct type, no remainder.
